title: Dynamical degrees of rational maps
summary: Graphs and topological degrees of dominant rational maps between projective varieties over an arbitrary field; Euler-characteristic intersection numbers with the positivity package over an arbitrary field (Kleiman, Siu, Hodge inequality, Khovanskii-Teissier, Siu for products); degrees deg_k(f; L, M) with model independence, positivity, normalization and field-extension invariance, sub-multiplicativity and comparison; dynamical degrees, log-concavity, birational and field-extension invariance, algebraic entropy; projective-space and affine-space examples (forms, morphisms, Cremona, Fibonacci, Frobenius, polynomial maps).

layers.title: Function fields and the graph of a dominant rational map

targets.name: RationalMap.functionFieldPullback / RationalMap.topologicalDegree
targets.statement: For a dominant K-rational map f : X ⤏ Y of varieties over K, f^* : K(Y) -> K(X) is the K-algebra map induced by RationalMap.fromFunctionField f (which hits the generic point of Y); e(f) = Module.finrank over f^*K(Y) of K(X). f |-> f^* is a bijection onto K-algebra maps K(Y) -> K(X); (g∘f)^* = f^*∘g^*; e(f) > 0 iff dim X = dim Y (junk 0 otherwise); e(g∘f) = e(f)e(g) in equal dimension; e(f) = 1 iff f^* is an isomorphism iff f is birational (the rational map of a partial isomorphism over K); then Scheme.Birational X Y holds and f^{-1} has pullback (f^*)^{-1}.
hypotheses: X, Y integral, separated, of finite type over K
f dominant and over Spec K
equal dimensions for finiteness and multiplicativity

locator.where: Definition 52.8 (tag 02NY), line 6046; dinhsibony2005 lines 69-70

api.name: topologicalDegree_eq_one_iff
api.statement: in equal dimension, e(f) = 1 iff f^* is an isomorphism iff f is the rational map of a partial isomorphism over K; then f^{-1} has pullback (f^*)^{-1}

targets.name: RationalMap.graph
targets.statement: For a K-rational map f : X ⤏ Y of projective varieties, Γ_f is the scheme-theoretic image of (ι_U, f_U) : U -> X ×_K Y, U = f.domain, with projections π_1, π_2. Γ_f is integral, closed, projective, of dimension dim X, independent of the representative; π_1 is a modification with witness U, π_1^{-1}(U) ≅ U; π_2 ∘ γ_f = f_U; f dominant implies π_2 surjective; equal dimensions make π_2 an alteration of generic degree e(f); morphisms give π_1 an isomorphism; birational inverses swap graphs.
hypotheses: X, Y projective varieties over K
f a K-rational map; dominant for the statements on π_2
dim X = dim Y for the alteration statement

Field extension: (Γ_f)_{K'} is the scheme-theoretic image of γ_f ×_K K'; for X, Y geometrically integral, f_{K'} is dominant, e(f_{K'}) = e(f), (g∘f)_{K'} = g_{K'}∘f_{K'}, Γ_{f_{K'}} = (Γ_f)_{K'}.

targets.name: LineBundle.IsNef
targets.statement: On a projective K-scheme, L is nef if (L·C) ≥ 0 for every integral closed curve C (on a projective variety this is ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII §0.1's nefness). Ample implies nef; nef is stable under sums, positive multiples, restriction and pullback; big and nef pulls back to big and nef along generically finite surjective maps of equal dimension with ((p^*L)^d) = deg(p)(L^d); nefness is invariant under field extension; nefness passes to W of §2.4.

gaps.title: nefness under extension of the ground field
gaps.detail: The field-extension part of the contract StableReductionPartII records for SchemeAndStackFoundations under the same name, in its forward direction on a projective integral K-scheme. §3.1 derives from it the converse and the statement for every projective K-scheme, and uses it to transport nefness to the integral variety over an algebraically closed field of §2.4.
gaps.needs: For a projective integral K-scheme X, a line bundle L on X and a field extension K'/K, if (L · C) ≥ 0 for every integral closed curve C ⊆ X, then (L_{K'} · C') ≥ 0 for every integral closed curve C' ⊆ X_{K'}.
